briefings.title: US and China: From Here to Where?
briefings.tldr: While deep structural forces continue to drive a fierce "Thucydidean" rivalry between the US and China, the bilateral summit has successfully established a temporary framework of "constructive strategic stability," allowing global businesses to navigate geopolitical volatility through highly localized strategies and targeted cooperation.

briefings.title: David Reich – Why the Bronze Age was an inflection point in human evolution
briefings.tldr: Overturning the scientific consensus that human evolution halted after the agricultural revolution, Harvard geneticist David Reich and collaborator Ali Akbari demonstrate that natural selection dramatically accelerated during the Bronze Age, driving massive shifts in immunity, metabolism, and a full standard deviation increase in genetic predictors of cognitive performance.

briefings.title: Rethinking Risk and Global Power with Jake Sullivan | The Outthinking Investor
briefings.tldr: The world has transitioned from the post-Cold War "unipolar moment" to an "old normal" of great power rivalry where economics and national security are inextricably linked, requiring the U.S. to move beyond punitive measures toward "offensive" economic statecraft like a national strategic investment fund.

briefings.title: Jason Furman on the Federal Reserve
briefings.tldr: Harvard Professor Jason Furman argues that Federal Reserve independence is essential for economic stability and warns that President Trump’s attempts to exert political control or fire governors could lead to higher inflation, market volatility, and a weakened U.S. dollar.

briefings.title: "Everything has changed" - Gita Gopinath on the global economy in 2026
briefings.tldr: Despite stable global growth numbers in 2025, Harvard economist Gita Gopinath warns that the global economy has fundamentally shifted, moving away from a predictable order due to escalating tariffs, a breakdown of trust between major alliances, and an AI boom whose financial valuations carry significant systemic risk.
